answer: Sybil resistance emerges when each autonomous agent anchors a verifiable kernel identity to a stake-slashing matrix, so duplicate identities pay a fixed penalty exceeding any double-signing reward. Nebula attestations bind nontransferable reputation to the kernel, while sonnet proofs compactly certify distinctness under zero-knowledge commitments. The resulting negative expected utility and capital lockup deter identity flooding and preserve Byzantine fault tolerance.
